title: Past Tense 5: Mixed Review
description: Synthesis of the whole past tense: regular formation, быть, tricky agreement, the irregular -чь / -ти families, and stress shifts. Four-step diagnostic: subject → family → ending → stress.
descriptionRussian: Повторение всего прошедшего времени: правильное образование, быть, трудное согласование, неправильные классы на -чь и -ти, сдвиги ударения.
intro: Everything from the last four lessons arrives together. Every past-tense form comes down to the same three questions, asked in order: who or what is the subject, does the verb belong to one of the irregular families, and which of the four endings does that leave you. Nothing today tells you which lesson a question came from.
rules: The four past-tense slots: -л (masc), -ла (fem), -ло (neut / impersonal), -ли (plural, polite вы, compound subjects).
Regular verbs: drop -ть, add the slot ending. Быть is regular in shape: был / была́ / бы́ло / бы́ли.
Irregular families: -чь (мог, лёг, пёк) and -ти / -сти (шёл, нёс, вёл) lose or reshape the masculine -л; other forms take regular endings.
examples: Маша читала книгу. (Masha was reading a book.) Regular, feminine: -ла.
Вы были в Москве? (Were you in Moscow? - polite.) Polite вы → plural были.
Папа был на работе. (Dad was at work.) Папа is masculine despite -а → был.
Антон шёл домой. (Anton was walking home.) -ти class, suppletive stem, masc шёл.
Лена жила́ в Петербурге. (Lena lived in Petersburg.) Stress-shift family, fem end-stressed жила́.
Вчера бы́ло холодно. (It was cold yesterday.) Impersonal → neuter бы́ло.

tables.title: The Whole Past Tense on One Page

items.hint: Recap from Lesson 1: regular verb, feminine subject.
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 1. Звонить is regular: drop -ть, add the slot ending. Лена is feminine singular → звонила. Today's drill mixes all five lessons.

items.promptEnglish: Were you at the meeting, Anna Petrovna?
items.hint: Step 1: the subject is polite вы.
items.explanation: Polite вы always takes the plural: Вы были (Lesson 3). The verb follows the pronoun's plural grammar even when you address one person.

items.promptEnglish: Anton was not able to help yesterday.
items.hint: Step 2: мочь is in the -чь family. What happens to the masculine -л?
items.explanation: Мочь is in the -чь class (Lesson 4): the masculine past is the bare stem мог, with no -л.

items.promptEnglish: Grandpa was reading the paper in the morning.
items.hint: Step 1: дедушка ends in -а, but who does it name?
items.explanation: Дедушка names a man, so it is masculine (Lesson 3): читал. The -а ending changes how the noun declines, not how the verb agrees.

items.promptEnglish: The children were walking home through the park.
items.hint: Step 2: the past of идти is built on a completely different stem. Step 1: plural subject.
items.explanation: Идти builds its past on a completely different stem, ш- (Lesson 4). Plural subject → шли.

blanks: Вчера _____ очень тепло, и мы гуляли весь день. (Yesterday it was very warm, and we walked all day.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: 'It was warm' is impersonal - no subject - so быть sits in the neuter: было (Lesson 2). The second verb гуляли is regular plural agreeing with мы.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha wrote grandma a long letter.
errorCorrection.explanation: Маша is feminine singular, so the past takes -ла: написала. The past tense agrees with the subject's gender, not with the speaker.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton was walking home through the park.
errorCorrection.explanation: Идти's past masculine is шёл - a single -л. Шёлл doubles the -л, which never happens in any past-tense form.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Who was in the classroom in the morning?
errorCorrection.explanation: Кто is grammatically masculine singular (Lesson 3): Кто был в классе? The verb agrees with кто itself, even if the expected answer is a group.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: It was cold in the morning and warm in the afternoon.
minimalPairs.explanation: Impersonal weather sentence: no subject, so neuter было. Была would need a feminine subject like зима.

patternRecognition.sentence: Вы были на концерте, Иван Сергеевич?
patternRecognition.question: Which rule explains the plural были for one man?
options: Polite вы always takes the plural verb
patternRecognition.answer: Polite вы always takes the plural verb
patternRecognition.explanation: The pronoun вы is grammatically plural even when politely addressing one person (Lesson 3), so the verb is plural: были.

patternRecognition.sentence: Антон мог помочь, а Лена не могла́.
patternRecognition.question: Why does the masculine form мог have no -л ending?
options: Мочь is in the -чь class: the masculine past is the bare stem
Мог is a future form, not a past form
It is a colloquial shortening of могл
patternRecognition.answer: Мочь is in the -чь class: the masculine past is the bare stem
patternRecognition.explanation: The -чь class (мочь, лечь, печь) forms its masculine past without -л: мог, лёг, пёк (Lesson 4). The feminine, neuter, and plural add the regular endings: могла́, могло́, могли́.

patternRecognition.sentence: На полке были книги и журналы.
patternRecognition.question: Which rule picks были in this 'there were' sentence?
options: Быть agrees with the things that existed, which are plural here
Полка is feminine, so the verb is plural
Lists of objects always take the neuter было
patternRecognition.answer: Быть agrees with the things that existed, which are plural here
patternRecognition.explanation: In 'there was / there were' sentences the existing things are the subject (Lesson 2). Книги и журналы is plural, so были. With one feminine thing it would be была: На полке была книга.

reviewVocab.definition: the four-step diagnostic for any past form: subject → family → ending → stress
reviewVocab.example: Шаг 1: подлежащее (Лена, женский род). Шаг 2: семья (жить — сдвиг ударения). Шаг 3: окончание (-ла). Шаг 4: ударение (жила́).

reviewVocab.definition: regular verb (standard past formation: drop -ть, add -л / -ла / -ло / -ли, no stress shift)
reviewVocab.example: Глагол 'читать' — правильный: читал / читала / читало / читали.

reviewVocab.definition: irregular verb (missing masculine -л, stem changes, or stress shifts; Lessons 4 and 5)
reviewVocab.example: Глагол 'мочь' — неправильный: мужская форма 'мог' не имеет окончания -л.
